Name: Disguise Undead
Description:
You make one undead—including its clothing, armor, weapons, and equipment—appear different until the spell ends or until you use your action to dismiss it. The spell also masks the scent of any decaying flesh that might emanate from the target. You can make the target seem 1 foot shorter or taller, and it can appear thin, fat, or anywhere in between. You cannot change its body type, so the illusion must preserve the same basic arrangement of limbs. Otherwise, the extent of the illusion is up to you. The illusion does not withstand physical inspection. For example:
● A hat placed on a zombie is intangible, revealing the rotting scalp beneath when touched.
● Illusory flesh added to a skeleton gives way when someone grasps its cold bones. A creature can use its action to inspect the target's appearance, making an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC. On a success, it discerns that the target is disguised.
At Higher Levels: When cast using a 3rd-level spell slot or higher, you may disguise one additional undead (each with a unique appearance) for every slot level above 3rd.
